effects: Authorizes EBSwap to settle the signer's leg of the swap whose full terms are committed in intentHash (token pair, EPKs, amount ciphertexts, expiry, salt; or for a public swap the public token, payer, recipient and publicAmount).

Binds the authorization to one exact transfer: transferParamsHash is keccak256 of the encrypted transfer params (atomicSwap / encrypted leg) or of the EIP-3009 ReceiveWithAuthorization terms (payer, EBSwap, publicAmount, validAfter, validBefore, nonce) for the public leg.

When the swap settles, the signer's tokenIn / encrypted / public-token amount leaves to the counterparty's receive EPK or publicRecipient, and the counterparty's leg arrives; this also needs the separate ZKEMT caller-bound transfer signature or EIP-3009 signature.
Consumes the signer's nonce in EBSwap's bitmap (_useAuthNonce); the signature is valid only while block.timestamp < deadline.
formats.shown: "Authorize swap" with two raw 32-byte hashes (swap intent hash, transfer params hash) and the authorization deadline as a date.

findings.title: SwapIntentAuth: tokens, amounts and counterparties are hidden inside intentHash and transferParamsHash.
findings.evidence: EBSwap.sol hashIntent: keccak256(abi.encode(intent)); _spendLeg: transferParamsHash = keccak256(abi.encode(params)); _publicTransferCommitment hashes publicPayer, address(this), publicAmount. The descriptor shows 'Swap intent hash' and 'Transfer params hash' as raw values only.
findings.fix: Nothing in the descriptor can fix this. A wallet can't decode the hashes. Signers have to check them against the dApp. A future message type could carry the swap terms in clear.

findings.title: SwapIntentAuth: two 32-byte hex hashes fill the screen, and a person cannot verify them.
findings.evidence: descriptor fields intentHash and transferParamsHash use format 'raw'; case 0 screen shows 0xcaca…ca and 0xffff…ff.
findings.fix: Keep them for checking against the dApp, but use labels that say so, e.g. 'Swap terms ID (check in app)'.

findings.title: SwapIntentAuth intent 'Authorize swap' does not say it approves the signer's own leg of an atomic swap.
findings.evidence: descriptor intent 'Authorize swap'; EBSwap._spendLeg consumes this signature and then calls IZKEMT(token).encryptedTransferWithCallerAuth for the signer's leg.
findings.fix: Use an intent like 'Authorize your side of an atomic swap', or add a short note that the amounts and tokens come from the swap terms shown in the app.

couldNotCheck: ZKEMT token encryptedTransferWithCallerAuth and the ZKHub controllers/isZkemt contracts are not in the directory. So I couldn't confirm from code that the signer's encrypted leg also needs the separate ZKEMT transfer signature before it moves.
